transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… what finally pushed me to come in is I can’t keep my focus the way I need to anymore. I’m an electrician, so a lot of my day is estimates, code forms, keeping track of what materials go with which job, that kind of thing—and lately I’ll sit down to finish one estimate and then a tool noise in the shop, or my phone buzzing, or even just some random new idea I get about reorganizing the workshop will pull me completely off track.

And then I’ll realize I’ve mixed up parts of two jobs, or I started a form and wandered off into something else before finishing it. It’s not just “oh, I got distracted once.” It’s been happening enough that it’s starting to mess with my work, and that’s what scared me into making the appointment.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, like you can't sit still?

Yeah—restless is probably the right word. I don’t know if it always looks like fidgeting exactly, but I feel like I’m constantly in motion. I’ll go from a job site to doing a bid, then back to the workshop to rewire some test panel I suddenly decided needs fixing, and then I’ll start sketching out some home-automation idea before I’ve even finished the last one.

It’s like sitting still feels… wrong, almost like I’m wasting time if I’m not doing something useful. Even when I’m supposed to just sit and finish paperwork, my body wants to get up and check tools, move materials around, start another task—something. It’s gotten to where I’m doing a lot, but not necessarily finishing it cleanly.
Did you have trouble with focus or restlessness when you were a kid?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I mean, I can think back and remember being a kid and not loving sitting still in class, but I don’t know if that was “trouble” in the way you mean, or just being a normal kid who wanted to be outside or doing something with his hands.

I don’t have, like, a clear memory of teachers constantly saying, “He can’t focus,” or anything that stands out strongly. School was kind of school—I got through it. I know I was always more interested in practical stuff, building things, taking things apart, that kind of thing, but I don’t know if I’d call that restlessness exactly.

So… I guess my answer is I’m not sure. It’s not something I’ve really thought about before, and nothing obvious is jumping out at me from childhood.
Did your parents or family members ever comment on your behavior or activity level when you were a child?

I honestly don’t remember them saying much in a clear way. Like, I’m trying to think of the exact kinds of comments my parents made, and nothing really specific comes to mind—nothing like, “You were bouncing off the walls,” or “You never sat still,” at least not that I can remember.

I mean, families say little things, you know? Like maybe I was “always busy” or I liked being outside or messing with stuff, but I don’t know if that was them describing a problem or just normal kid stuff. My dad was pretty practical too, so if I was taking something apart or helping with a project, that might’ve just been seen as useful, not hyperactive or anything.

So… I don’t want to say no for sure, because maybe they did and I just didn’t register it, but I don’t have a strong memory of my family making comments about my activity level being unusual.
Do you think your difficulty with focus and restlessness have been present throughout your life, or did they start more recently?

I’d say it’s more recent. Not like it started yesterday or anything, but when I look back, the last… maybe seven months or so is when it really started building.

It lines up pretty closely with when we took on the mortgage for the workshop and the equipment. That was a big step, and since then it’s felt like my brain just doesn’t shut off the same way. Before that I could be busy, sure, and I’ve always liked having projects going, but this level of being pulled from one thing to the next and feeling like I can’t settle—this feels like it’s been ramping up since then.

So I wouldn’t say it’s been exactly the same my whole life. I don’t have that clear childhood-to-now pattern. It feels more like something that’s grown over the past several months, especially with the pressure of the workshop and equipment hanging over me.
Have these difficulties with focus and restlessness caused you significant distress or problems in your daily life beyond just the issues at work?

Yeah… I think it has. I wish I could say it’s just work stress and it stays at the shop, but it doesn’t. It’s starting to spill into everything.

At work, clients have been catching things I should’ve caught—missed details, wrong notes, scheduling stuff getting mixed up. And that’s embarrassing, because in my line of work you’re supposed to be solid. People are trusting you to know what’s happening and keep things straight. I’ve had a couple clients complain, not just casually mention it, but actually be frustrated with me. That gets in my head.

And with my apprentices… I can feel it there too. They used to just kind of follow my lead, and now I can tell they’re second-guessing me. Like if I tell them where we’re supposed to be or what needs to happen next, there’s this hesitation, like they’re wondering if I’ve got it right. That bothers me more than I expected, honestly, because I don’t want to be the guy people have to work around.

At home it’s been rough too. The mortgage, the business, the equipment—all of that has turned into this constant argument with my wife. She feels like I’m putting everything we built at risk, and I get why she says that, even if I don’t like hearing it. It’s like we can’t talk about normal things without it circling back to money or the shop or whether I’m handling things the right way.

So yes, it’s causing problems. It’s not just me feeling distracted. It’s affecting people’s trust in me, and it’s affecting my marriage.
Did you experience any of these focus or restlessness issues before the age of 12?

No, not that I can really point to. I don’t remember having this kind of focus problem or restlessness before I was 12.

I mean, I was a kid, so I’m sure I had normal kid energy, but this thing I’m talking about now feels different. It’s been building more in the last seven months or so, since we took on the mortgage for the workshop and the equipment. That’s when I started noticing it as something that was actually affecting me, not something I remember being part of my childhood.
Are you certain you didn't experience any symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity before the age of 12?

I mean… as certain as I can be, looking back that far. I don’t have some perfect memory of being a kid, so I don’t want to say it like I’ve reviewed every moment of my childhood. But no, I can’t really identify this same kind of thing before age 12.

What I’m dealing with now feels tied to the last several months. It’s been building for about seven months, since we took on the mortgage for the workshop and the equipment. That’s when I really noticed my focus and restlessness becoming something I couldn’t just brush off or explain as normal busyness.

Before that, I’m sure I had normal kid energy or got distracted sometimes like anyone, but I don’t remember it being this pattern or this level of problem. The clear change, to me, is much more recent.
Are you certain that you didn't experience any symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity at any point before the age of 7?

Before age 7? I really don’t think so. I know I’ve said something similar already, but when I try to look back that far, I just don’t have a memory of being that kind of distracted or restless as a little kid in a way that stood out.

What I can say pretty clearly is that this current thing has been building for about seven months. It started becoming noticeable after we took on the mortgage for the workshop and the equipment, and that’s when it went from just normal stress or being busy to something I actually felt was affecting me day to day.

So, no—I can’t honestly point to anything before age 7. The timeline that makes sense to me is much more recent, around those last seven months.
Have you experienced any other mental health issues, such as depression or anxiety, around the same time as these focus and restlessness problems started?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I’ve been stressed, definitely, and the timing kind of overlaps because the focus and restlessness stuff started around a period where there was more pressure in general. But as far as whether it was like a separate depression or anxiety issue… I don’t know.

I haven’t really thought of it that way. I guess I’d need you to explain what you mean a little more, because I don’t want to say yes to something if what I’m describing is just being overwhelmed or under pressure. I’ve noticed the focus and restlessness more clearly than anything else.
Do you think your focus and restlessness issues might be related to feeling overwhelmed or anxious about your work and personal life situation?

It might be, yeah… I mean, I can see how it could be connected. I just don’t know how to separate it out neatly.

Work and personal stuff have felt like a lot, and when there’s that kind of pressure, I do notice I get more keyed up and it’s harder to settle into one thing. But I’m not sure if that means I’m anxious in the way you’re asking, or if I’m just reacting to having too much on my plate. Like, I don’t want to overstate it and say, “Yes, it’s definitely anxiety,” because I’m not totally sure that’s what it is.

What I do know is that when I feel overwhelmed, the focus issues and restlessness seem harder to ignore. Whether that’s the cause, or it’s just making something else worse, I honestly don’t know.
Are you completely certain you didn't experience any symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity at any point before your 12th birthday?

Completely certain? I don’t know if I can say completely certain, just because that’s a long time ago and memory gets fuzzy. Before 12 is still pretty far back.

But I don’t really remember having those kinds of problems then. I wasn’t thinking of myself as a kid who couldn’t sit still or couldn’t pay attention, at least not in any way that stands out to me now. I’m trying to be careful, because maybe there were normal kid moments—getting bored, not wanting to do homework, whatever—but nothing that I can point to and say, “Yes, that was a real pattern before I turned 12.”

So I guess my honest answer is: I’m not completely certain in the absolute sense, but I don’t have a clear memory of inattention or hyperactivity being an issue before my 12th birthday.
Are you certain you didn't experience any symptoms of inattention before the age of 12?

I wouldn’t say I’m certain in the way you’re asking, no. I mean, I don’t have some clear record in my head from being 8 or 9 years old where I can confidently say, “No, that never happened.” That feels too absolute.

What I can say is I don’t remember inattention being a major issue before 12. I don’t have a strong memory of teachers constantly saying I couldn’t focus, or me feeling like I was always unable to pay attention in a way that stood out. But childhood memories are kind of blurry, and I’m also aware that sometimes you don’t label things that way when you’re a kid.

So… no, I’m not certain. I just don’t have anything specific I can point to from before age 12 that makes me think, yes, that was definitely happening then.
Did you exhibit any symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity between the ages of 7 and 12?

I honestly don’t know that I can say yes to that. Between 7 and 12, I don’t have a clear memory of having ongoing inattention or hyperactivity symptoms. Like, I’m trying to picture myself at that age—school, being in class, doing homework—and nothing really stands out as a pattern.

I’m sure I had normal kid stuff, like getting bored or not wanting to sit through something, but I don’t remember it being something people were worried about or something that caused a lot of problems. I don’t remember thinking, “I can’t focus,” or being told all the time that I was too restless.

So I guess my answer is: not that I can clearly remember. I wouldn’t want to swear there was absolutely nothing, because I was a kid and it’s hard to know, but I don’t have anything specific from ages 7 to 12 that I’d point to and say, yeah, that was definitely happening.
Do you recall your parents or anyone else mentioning that you had trouble paying attention or sitting still when you were really young, like before you started school?

I don’t really recall anyone saying that, no. I mean, before I started school is especially hard for me to know, because that’s like… I’d mostly be relying on stories other people told me later, not my own memory.

I don’t remember my parents describing me as a kid who couldn’t sit still or couldn’t pay attention, at least not in a way that stuck with me. They might’ve said normal little-kid things, like I was energetic or got into things, but I don’t remember anyone framing it as a problem or saying, “You were always impossible to manage,” or anything like that.

So I guess the honest answer is I don’t have a specific memory of anyone mentioning that about me from before school age. It’s possible there were comments here and there that I just don’t remember, but nothing clear comes to mind.
Did any symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity cause significant problems for you before you were 12 years old?

I don’t think so, no—not that I can clearly point to. I’m trying to be careful because “significant problems” sounds like something that would have shown up pretty clearly, like teachers calling home a lot, me constantly getting in trouble, failing things because I couldn’t pay attention, or my parents really worrying about me not being able to sit still. And I don’t remember that being the case before I was 12.

I mean, I’m sure I had moments where I was distracted or restless, because I was a kid, and I don’t want to make it sound like I was perfectly focused all the time. But if you’re asking whether it caused major problems in school or at home, I don’t have any memory of that. Nothing stands out to me as a pattern or as something people treated like a real issue back then.

So my best answer is: I don’t recall any significant problems from inattention or hyperactivity before age 12. I can’t say it’s impossible, but I don’t have anything solid to give you there.
Were you experiencing any symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity as an adult before the last seven months?

Before the last seven months? I’m not really sure I’d say I was experiencing that, at least not in a way that I noticed as a clear thing.

I mean, I’ve had times as an adult where I got distracted or procrastinated or had a hard time staying on top of stuff, but I always kind of thought of that as normal life stress, or being tired, or just not wanting to do paperwork or chores after work. I don’t remember it being this obvious pattern where I was like, “Something is wrong with my attention,” or where people were constantly pointing out that I couldn’t sit still.

With work especially, I’ve usually had to stay pretty focused because being an electrician, you can’t really be careless. So if you’re asking whether I had ongoing inattention or hyperactivity symptoms before the last seven months, I don’t have a solid example. I wouldn’t want to say absolutely never, because I’m sure there were moments, but nothing stands out to me as a major or consistent problem before then.
Did you experience any symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity as an adult before the last seven months?

Right, yeah—I know I kind of answered that already, but I guess the short version is: not really in any clear way that I can identify.

Like, as an adult before these last several months, I’m sure I had normal distracted moments. I’d lose track of something here or there, put off boring tasks, maybe feel antsy if I had to sit through something long. But I didn’t think of it as a pattern, and I don’t remember it causing real problems or people telling me, “You’re always all over the place,” or anything like that.

Especially with work, I’ve generally been able to keep myself on task when I needed to. So I’m hesitant to say I had symptoms, because nothing really stands out to me from before the last seven months as a consistent inattention or hyperactivity issue.
Did any symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity start before you were 12 years old?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’m trying to really think back to before middle school, and nothing jumps out at me as, like, “Oh yeah, that was already happening then.”

I was a kid, so I’m sure I got distracted sometimes or had energy like any kid would, but I don’t remember it being a thing where teachers were concerned, or my parents were always being told I couldn’t pay attention, or I was constantly in trouble for being too restless. If it had been a major pattern, I feel like I’d remember someone making a big deal out of it.

So no, as far as I know, symptoms like that did not start before I was 12. I can’t swear there were zero moments, but I don’t have anything solid from that age that I’d point to.
Do you recall having any trouble paying attention or sitting still before you started school?

Before I started school? Honestly, I don’t really know. That’s far enough back that I don’t have a clear memory of myself in that way.

I can remember little bits and pieces from being really young, like playing at home or being with family, but I don’t remember whether I had trouble paying attention or sitting still in any kind of meaningful pattern. And I don’t recall my parents ever telling me later, like, “You were impossible to keep still,” or “You could never focus,” anything like that.

So I guess my answer would be: I’m not aware of that being an issue before school. I can’t really say for sure because I was so young, but nothing has ever stood out to me or been brought up as a problem from that time.
